## 2\. The higher-rank obstacle survives exact class decomposition

The actual reachable class can be represented effectively as a semilinear set. This follows from the existing theory of cyclic Petri nets, because weak reversibility makes every reachable population capable of returning to its initial state. The effective-semilinearity theorem supplies a finite arithmetic description of \(\Gamma\)\. citeturn590764search8

That resolves an important representation issue, but not the spectral question. Even on a semilinear class, the Dirichlet form involves infinitely many factorial-weighted edges, and a finite arithmetic description of those edges does not automatically yield a uniform coercivity constant.

I examined whether the remaining infinite-state question could be reduced to asymptotic zeros of the reaction polynomials

\[
P_r(u)=u^{z_r}-u^{y_r}.
\]

For the full orthant, an escaping sequence with

\[
\|u_n\|\longrightarrow\infty,\qquad
\sum_r|P_r(u_n)|^2\longrightarrow0
\]

certifies zero gap by the accepted character formula.

An exact simplification is that allowing complex \(u_n\) does not strengthen this particular sufficient test: replacing each coordinate by its modulus preserves escape and satisfies

\[
\left||u_n|^{z_r}-|u_n|^{y_r}\right|
\leq |u_n^{z_r}-u_n^{y_r}|.
\]

Thus this escape test can be formulated over positive real variables and decided by real quantifier elimination.

**The necessary direction remains unproved.** I cannot establish that every zero-gap sequence of arbitrary form-domain functions must produce such an escaping polynomial character, even on the full orthant. For a proper reachable class, the class projection introduces an additional obstruction.

The Fock-space polynomial-operator results of Haslinger also do not establish that missing implication: their coercivity statements require operator and commutator hypotheses that are not automatic for the reaction-polynomial row. citeturn558608view0

## 3\. Why the available procedures do not constitute a total algorithm

The accepted finite-support core and pinned-gap theorem already give a program that produces certified witnesses for every zero-gap input. The EDA finite-cut method supplies an additional structural family of such certificates. The rank-one result above supplies another class of positive instances with rational lower bounds.

For arbitrary higher-rank networks, however, the following implication has not been established\:

\[
\lambda>0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\text{an effectively discoverable finite full-domain
coercivity certificate}.
\]

Nor is there a proved converse characterizing all zero-gap inputs through a bounded family of algebraic, path or finite-cut certificates.

Without one of these completeness results, dovetailing the existing tests is not a terminating algorithm: a zero-gap instance may evade every selected structural test, while a positive-gap instance can have finite truncations with small but strictly positive Rayleigh quotients.

The published positive path-comparison theorem of Anderson–Cappelletti–Fan–Kim and the negative active-cycle criteria of Kim–Kim retain their respective sufficient scopes. Neither supplies the required exhaustive dichotomy. citeturn118894view0turn118894view1

## Final determination

The rank-one extension establishes an additional fully positive class, including arbitrary species counts and molecularities. Effective class representations and the existing zero-gap certificates remain available.

But for unrestricted stoichiometric rank and arbitrary linkage classes\:

- No uniform terminating positive-versus-zero decision algorithm has been constructed.
- No full-domain rational Poincaré lower-bound procedure has been established for every positive-gap input.
- No exact-model undecidability reduction has been proved.
- Consequently, the requested universal bit-complexity bounds cannot be justified.

**The full physical-time Poincaré-gap decidability problem remains unresolved in this investigation.** The new rank-one theorem is a valid restricted result, not a resolution of the quantified problem.
